title: Basin of Vows
snippet:
Basin of Vows -  Dark Souls III - item - lead 
 lead : The **Basin of Vows** is a key item in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Basin of Vows
snippet:

 usage : Approaching the beheading statue behind Emma's chair with the Basin of Vows in hand will trigger the Dancer of the Boreal Valley fight.

Once the Dancer has been defeated, interacting with the beheading statue will place the basin in front of it, triggering a cutscene that unlocks access to Lothric Castle.

title: Black Firebomb
snippet:
Black Firebomb -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : **Black Firebombs** are offensive items in *Dark Souls*. They are projectile weapons and are more powerful variants of Firebombs.

title: Black Firebomb
snippet:

title: Black Firebomb
snippet:
Black Firebomb -  Dark Souls - item - overview 
 overview : Black Firebombs are very powerful early in the game. The damage they deal is enough to make them competitive as useful utility items throughout the middle of the game. However, at higher levels their relative damage may be considered lackluster.

title: Black Firebomb
snippet:
Black Firebomb -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Black firebombs have a flat fire attack of 250.

Black Firebombs as one's starting gift are a particularly reliable method to defeat the Asylum Demon on a first playthrough and obtain the Demon's Great Hammer.

title: Charcoal Pine Resin
snippet:
Charcoal Pine Resin -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Charcoal Pine Resin may only be used on enchantable weapons upgraded down the Standard, Raw, or Crystal paths, as well as a limited amount of exceptions.

The Charcoal Pine Resin adds a flat 80 fire attack to the right-hand weapon for one minute. Switching weapons after using Charcoal Pine Resin will cause its effect to end.

The Charcoal Pine Resin is the weakest weapon augmentation in the game; however, it has no requirements and is more easily obtained than the Gold Pine Resin.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Killing Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle in order to obtain the basin has no negative storyline consequences, as the player will still be summoned to the cathedral by her after defeating the third Lord of Cinder. However, Lion Knight Albert's summon will become unavailable, as he will use his Black Separation Crystal to leave if Emma dies.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet: Around half health, the Dancer will bring out her second blade which does Magic damage, losing her ability to perform her grab attack. Her combos become much more dangerous and lengthy at this point, with several of them having unpredictable stopping points (particularly her twirl) or retaliatory follow-ups to punish attempts to attack at the end of a combo. During this phase, it is generally better to stay in front of her rather than behind, in order to more easily read her attacks and dodge. Be mindful that her twirling attacks coincide precisely with chained rolls, so performing repeated rolls at the right moment will dodge all of them including the finishing spin. The few chains that she does throw however can leave behind a dragging trail of fire, or dark. That tracks through the attacks path.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : The Dancer is a towering, lanky being that closely resembles the Boreal Outrider Knights, beastly armored knights from Irithyll with silver and slim armor. She also wears a crown with a long mirage-like veil, an article that proves her direct lineage from the old royal family of the gods. Instead of crawling on all fours like the other Boreal Knights, she stands with her torso bent forward and her back curved, fighting and moving like she's dancing with deceptively slow steps.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : In Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, several ghosts of long dead knights can be seen wandering along the city streets. Two unique ghosts in particular, one male and the other female, can be seen departing from the cathedral at the end of the main street. They heavily resemble Vordt and the Dancer, both of whom served together under Pontiff Sulyvahn's command.
In the network test and early demos, the Dancer's name appeared as the "Dancer of the Frigid Valley".
An unused set of audio files can be found that depict the Dancer laughing and shrilling as she enters the fight, as well as giving a haunting chuckle when she stares at the player. This laughter and shrill is of a multi-voiced female source.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
The Dancer is weak to Strike and Dark damage, as well as being susceptible to Bleed buildup. This makes Human Pine Resin and Carthus Rouge powerful tools to use for this fight, as well as weapons such as the Dark Hand. Casters will have the option to use spells such as Dorhys' Gnawing and Great Deep Soul, which will allow them to eviscerate her from a distance.

Keep in mind that the Dancer's attacks are often lanky and very difficult to telegraph. So the player should take caution when choosing a time to attack.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Dancer of the Boreal Valley** is a boss in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The arena in which the Dancer is fought is not very large, and gives limited room for avoiding her attacks. As well, the furniture at the sides can obstruct movement, so rolling through them early in the fight can provide more maneuvering space later. The pillars at the sides can also be used as a limited form of cover to shield oneself from her attacks. These pillars as well as the walls can be set on fire by hitting them with a Fire source like the torch, or by the Dancer's attacks with her right-hand weapon.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Dancer is a direct descendant of Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight. She was among the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans, who inhabit Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city built for them on the ruins of Anor Londo.

After Sulyvahn imprisoned Dark Sun Gwyndolin, proclaimed himself pontiff and assumed control of the city, he bestowed upon the Dancer a set of paired enchanted swords. A symbol of her subjugation by the tyrant, the twinblades were enchanted with dark magic in the right-hand and fire in the left, mirroring those of the Pontiff. She was then ordered to serve Sulyvahn as a "dancer".

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet: The Dancer is not a particularly fast boss, but her movements are deliberate and she has very long and powerful combos, so fast weapons that do not have long windup or recovery times can work better than slow and powerful weapons. She also does not have a lot of health for a boss at this stage of the game, reducing her difficulty for experienced players attempting to kill her early. She will eventually stagger after taking enough Poise damage, and enough hits targeted on her head will open her up for a critical attack. A relatively heavy armor set and strong enough two handed weapon can stagger her in about 2 to 3 strikes. Though the stagger state only last for around 2.5 seconds and will only offer the enhance damage effect for around half as much time.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet: For the first phase of the fight, the Dancer performs limited combos with her weapon, with a few attacks that can reach her sides or behind her. It is best to stay near the Dancer's right leg so that her grab is easier to see (although it doesn't reach far, it can reach far around her left side, making it a bad idea to side roll). Boosting fire resistance with the Flame Stoneplate Ring or Red Bug Pellet may be a good idea but not required as it is in your best interest to avoid her attacks altogether. Using stamina reinforcers like the Grass Crest Shield, Chloranthy Ring, or Green Blossoms are a good idea, as it will provide more stamina to be ready to evade her attacks.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn ordered the Dancer to serve as a Boreal Outrider Knight, equivalent to being exiled. These knights, before being dispatched to foreign lands, were given the eye rings of the Pontiff, which eventually transformed them into savage, raving warriors who only knew how to serve as mindless guards, which ensured Sulyvahn's total control over the knights and deprived them of any means of desertion.

The Dancer was sent to Lothric together with a division of Boreal Outrider Knights under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here she positioned herself to guard the Cathedral and High Priestess Emma. Like other Outrider Knights, she would end up transformed into a frenzied beast by the rings of the Pontiff, causing her armor to be fused with her hide.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the Dancer, in particular, was sent to Lothric in response to the priestess' request for help.
**The Dancer was a direct descendant of Gwynevere, former queen of Lothric, which meant that she could have had some claim over the throne of Lothric. In the event of the demise of Lorian and Lothric, Sulyvahn had in place a figure with legitimacy to inherit the throne as the step-sibling to the heirs. With King Oceiros gone mad and the Queen vanished, there were no other known contenders with royal blood. Sulyvahn, by officially marrying the "dancer" at his service, could reasonably become king consort of Lothric.

title: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Dancer of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - location 
 location : Found in the High Wall of Lothric, in the cathedral where Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle resides. Under normal circumstances, she will reveal herself after the player has defeated the first three Lords of Cinder: the Abyss Watchers, Aldrich, Saint of the Deep and Yhorm the Giant.

After the third Lord of Cinder has been defeated, a cutscene will play with Emma summoning the Ashen One to the cathedral. Once there, she will bestow them the Basin of Vows. Walking up to the statue of the beheading knight behind her with it in possession will trigger the boss fight.

Alternatively, the player may kill Emma at any time during the game, loot the basin from her body and approach the statue to commence the battle. This allows for early access to Lothric Castle, the Consumed King's Garden and Untended Graves.

title: Firebomb
snippet:
Firebomb -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : When used, the player throws the firebomb in the direction they are facing or at the enemy targeted, which has a fire attack of 180. The throw distance is very long, but is hindered by the lack of precision at a distance due to the lack of a lock-on option at a distance. Black Firebombs are more powerful versions of firebombs.

Firebombs are one of only a handful of ranged attacks that don't suffer from damage drop-off from long-range throws. This, and the fact that they only explode on contact, makes them very useful for taking out enemies from long range. However, aiming may prove problematic.

snippet:
Hellkite Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - attacks 
 attacks : {'name': 'Jumping Flame Dash', 'description': 'The Hellkite Drake hovers in the air, and then dashes towards the player, whilst exhaling flame on the bridge. Can only be avoided by descending the stairs in the middle of the bridge.'}

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Hellkite Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : It is possible to prevent the Drake appearing at all if the player has the Master Key. Taking the shortcut next to the elevator in New Londo Ruins leads to the Valley of Drakes, then going past the Undead Dragon and a pair of Blue Drakes leads to an elevator to Darkroot Garden by a bonfire by a Halberd Black Knight that guards the Grass Crest Shield, at which point the player can choose to go up Havel's watchtower to go to Undead Burg or continue going up Darkroot Garden and go past the Undead Parish Titanite Demon by Andre of Astora to be in the Parish proper. By doing this, the player bypasses the event trigger at the beginning of the Undead Burg just past the first fog door where the Drake shortly perches. This event can still be triggered at any point.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Lightning Spear, earned through participation in the Warrior of Sunlight covenant, can inflict very strong damage against the drake.
If at the end of the bridge near Solaire of Astora, one can provoke the drake to fly in by walking a few meters on the bridge then sprinting back to safety. While the drake is on the bridge, if the player travels far enough towards Solaire, the drake will lose interest, turn around, and return to its perch. It is possible to walk back and forth causing the drake to alternate between turning to face the player and turning away. As it paces back and forth, the drake is unable to heal or attack. By doing this, the player can then slowly kill it with arrows while it turns uselessly. This threshold is particularly easy to work with headshots from the Black Bow of Pharis with the Hawk Ring equipped.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet: It is possible to kill the Hellkite Drake before the player has reached the Undead Parish safely with a bow, however you will need to use a three shot cycle while standing on the edge of the walkway under the bridge. Standing on the opposite side you would use to acquire the Drake Sword.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Hellkite Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : The Hellkite Drake is a reference to the Red Dragon from *Demon's Souls*, which attacks and harasses the player using fire breath attacks in Worlds 1-1 and 1-2 of Boletarian Palace.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Wait for the Hellkite Drake to land on the bridge as described above and fight with melee. The Drake regenerates health after it has about 33% HP left, should it still be on its perch; this makes approaches that only use bows and arrows ineffective.
Builds with high Strength and Dexterity can use a Dragonslayer Greatbow (or Gough's Greatbow) with an equipped Hawk Ring to dispatch it from a distance. This is will cost a considerable amount of souls as both types of ammo are expensive.
Lightning Spear, earned through participation in the Warrior of Sunlight covenant, can inflict very strong damage against the drake.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Upon initial encounter, it is worth attempting to attack the Hellkite Drake's tail, as cutting off its tail will grant the player the Drake Sword, which is a weapon without any kind of scaling. The most reliable way to do this is to equip a bow and shoot at its tail with arrows. Dealing enough damage to the tail will cause it to fall off and grant the player the sword.

Should the player return to this area later in the game, there are a few ways to permanently dispatch the Hellkite Drake:

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Hellkite Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : The Hellkite Drake attacks the player on the bridge leading to the Undead Parish, although it makes a brief appearance when the player first enters the Undead Burg. It guards the bridge until it is killed. If the player avoids it and runs to the Sunlight Altar bonfire behind it, the drake will fly off, and may return when the player attempts to cross the bridge again.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
In order to progress into the Undead Parish, the player has two options:

Run across the bridge hugging the right hand side, go down the stairs to the right and kick down the ladder that leads to the Undead Burg Bonfire. Go back up to the bridge and wait in the safe pockets that are on either side of the bridge. Watch the Hellkite Drake and wait a moment. The Drake will land on the bridge and players can run right past it to Sunlight Altar Bonfire located in the room directly below where the Drake perches.
There is a route underneath the bridge, close to the shortcut to the Undead Burg bonfire. It is guarded by two Hollow Soldiers and several Undead Rats. This route has no rest points until one reaches the bonfire close to Andre of Astora, so it is more punishing should the player die en route to their objective.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Hellkite Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - lead 
 lead : The , also known as the **Red Drake** or **Bridge Wyvern**, is a miniboss in *Dark Souls*.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Hellkite Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : The Hellkite Drake is said to be a flawed Dragon. Drakes are seen as underdeveloped imitators of the ancient dragons, but are more likely their distant kin.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
Hellkite Drake -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : In general, the Hellkite Drake is not meant to be fought directly when encountered on the bridge, as it is far stronger than the player. Rather, the best course of action is to avoid engaging it until returning much later with better stats and upgraded weapons.

In order to progress into the Undead Parish, the player has two options:

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Though Vordt can't close gaps instantly, he is still capable of charging over open terrain. If he lowers himself closer to the ground, he will likely charge the player, at which point the attack can be typically be dodged as easily as running to either side.

When down to about half health, Vordt will be surrounded by a glittering mist. He will then use a charge attack which he repeats three times in a row, dashing from one side of the arena to the other, and then back and forth. Attempting to block may lead to death, as the back-to-back charges deal substantial damage. Dodging is the most efficient way to avoid these attacks.

Now is your cue to change tactics. Be aggressive after each charge burst, three hits then roll away. Rinse and repeat this strategy until he begins to load up his freeze breath, now you must run round behind him and punish as much as you can. Using this strategy the fight will be over in no time.

**His mask, however, was originally going to be an item given to the player upon defeating him, but was cut from the game before release. Its model can be seen in the unused files of the game.

 lead : **Vordt of the Boreal Valley** is a boss in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet: After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Vordt was sent to Lothric with a division of Boreal Outrider Knights, with orders to keep a watchful eye over the Dancer of the Boreal Valley. title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Vordt of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - summons 
 summons : Lion Knight Albert - His summon sign is located just before the stairs leading to the boss arena (only if High Priestess Emma is still alive).
Sword Master - If the player has defeated the Sword Master at Firelink Shrine, his summon sign will appear just before the entrance to the arena.

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
He also uses a new ability after each set of charges. At the end of the third charge, he will stomp and take a deep breath of icy air and breath it out as a stream of ice that damages the player and inflicts Frost. This ability is cast horizontally left-to-right across his body. Standing behind Vordt will allow the player to attack him while avoiding the Frost effect.

Vordt starts using new attacks during the second half of the fight, including several small, faster strikes. The faster strikes are easier to block but they can still easily break the player's guard without sufficient care for stamina management.

Often, rolling directly underneath Vordt works well for avoiding his big attacks. However, staying there may cause him to perform a body slam.

Although Vordt is found too early in the game for the player to get any substantial Frost resistance; in future NG+ playthroughs, achieving higher frost resistance helps avoid Frostbite status.

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Vordt of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Vordt spends the first half of the fight making sweeping attacks and overhead strikes. These are well telegraphed, so the window for dodging is quite large. Blocking these attacks may lead to large stamina loss, meaning dodging is often more viable.

Attacking in short bursts may prove more effective, as it allows the player to deal sufficient damage and keep enough stamina to dodge away.

Vordt's AI does not know what to do if you get directly behind him. If you take advantage of this after each charge in phase one then you can get him into a loop of trying to turn and face you. His turns have gaps in between them that give you the chance to put in some punishment. By staying at his rear you can end the first phase quickly with no hits taken.

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet:
Vordt of the Boreal Valley -  Dark Souls III - boss - location 
 location : Found at the bottom of the High Wall of Lothric, opposite to the castle and near the gate leading outside the city, toward the Undead Settlement.

title: Warrior (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The starting Round Shield has good Stability and surprisingly good physical blocking for a wooden shield, but unless the user wishes to Parry it is best exchanged for the Silver Eagle Kite Shield found in High Wall of Lothric to get a 100% physical blocking shield instead and will let them use skills more frequently thanks to the Weapon Skill Weapon Art.

Its Northern Set has good physical defence but is severely lacking in all elemental defences except for fire and has above average resistances, especially against Frost.

An already infused version of the Battle Axe can be found in the High Wall of Lothric. While this weapon is guarded by a strong monster, the split Physical and Dark damage of its Deep infusion can be enough to overwhelm early-game enemies defences and the second boss, Vordt, is weak to Dark damage, as is the Demon found in the area after him. While this won't last through the game, it is a good replacement for a bit until the original weapon can be upgraded more.

title: Warrior (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Battle Axe is a strong weapon, if a bit slow, and thanks to its good Strength-scaling it will gain extra damage when two-handed. Its Weapon Art, Warcry, boosts the Axe's damage by roughly 10% for 30 seconds and turns the heavy attack and charged heavy attack into running charge attacks. This is a weapon buff and as such doesn't stack with spells such as Magic Weapon or items such as Charcoal Pine Resin, but since it boosts the weapon's base damage it can ignore the problems the other, elemental damage-focused options can get with having to bypass several different defences by instead focusing purely on physical damage. Be aware that due to the Warrior's low starting attunement it is only initially possible to get 3 uses of Warcry without either leveling Attunement by at least 2 points more or by carrying an Ashen Estus Flask.

title: Warrior (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Warrior (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Warrior** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Strength-focused class, with good Vigor for extra health and a decent amount of Endurance and Luck for more Stamina and Item Discovery. It does, however, have fairly low Dexterity and casting stats, with its very low Attunement of 6 making it notable for being the only starting class that doesn't immediately have an attunement slot for spells.

snippet:
Anor Londo (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Unlike its Dark Souls counterpart, Anor Londo's illusionary shining sun is gone and has been replaced with the cold blue rays of the moon. The city has noticeably frozen over, as well as being severely reduced in size, with the only remaining parts of the old city being the cathedral, the rotating staircase, and the honorary tomb of Gwyn. An additional tower now stands where the entrance of the building housing the Painted World of Ariamis once stood, with an invisible walkway leading to the top. Additionally, only three of the Silver Knights remain and all Batwing Demons are gone. The cathedral has been overrun by Deacons of the Cathedral of the Deep and Writhing Rotten Flesh. The inside of the cathedral has been covered in corpses and maggots. The eastern section of the cathedral has been blocked off by debris, but the western section is still accessible and contains the body of an old blacksmith.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: After Aldrich linked the Flame, a cult formed around his figure, but the deacons of the cathedral also found themselves fighting abominations that emerged from the Deep. The Cathedral, once a peaceful and sacred place for purification, was corrupted by the foul Aldrich, as darkness stagnated and accumulated in the Deep until it had become the final rest of abhorrent creatures. McDonnell found delight in the stagnation of darkness and abandoned his faith in the First Flame and in the gods, devoting himself to the Deep. He spread his belief among the clerics of the cathedral; he even created staffs that channeled faith to produce Deep sorceries, a sacrilegious act. In time the cathedral's deacons became both clergymen and sorcerers, embracing the cult of the Deep and the worship of its Saint, Aldrich.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : McDonnell, along with Archdeacons Royce and Klimt, was an archdeacon of the Way of White. The three men managed the Cathedral of the Deep, overseeing its rituals of purification from stagnant Darkness.

At one point, the cathedral welcomed Aldrich, an exiled Irithyllian priest who derived pleasure from eating humans. Aldrich shared his perverse behaviour with others in the cathedral, and sacrifices were brought to him to appease his hunger and grant him the strength to link the First Flame and become a Lord of Cinder.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : Archdeacon McDonnell's remains can be found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, at the Water Reserve.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward until reaching the building at the end of the big courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering, hit the left wall to uncover an illusory wall. Descend the ladder and dispose of the two Sulyvahn's Beasts waiting at the bottom. Archdeacon McDonnell's remains are located at the far-left corner of the hall, near the Water Reserve bonfire, which will appear once both beasts have been defeated.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Archdeacon McDonnell**, or **McDonnell of the Boreal Valley**, is a character in *Dark Souls III*. Praying to his remains allows access to the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: At some point McDonnell was incapacitated and his body ended up in the lower levels of Irithyll, in a cistern guarded by two of Pontiff Sulyvahn's beasts, however he is still able to recognize others, as he manages Aldrich's covenant and teaches sorceries.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Archdeacon McDonnell, a sorcerer himself, delighted in the cathedral's stagnating souls. For him, they represented the glorious bedrock of this world.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: Armor (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Armor (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - upgrading 
 upgrading : Like weapons, most but not all armor pieces can be upgraded. Armor can be upgraded to +10 or to +5 for those that require Twinkling Titanite. Armor cannot be upgraded down other upgrade paths. Upgraded armor yields higher defensive values and elemental resistance, but never alters Poise.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet:
Champion Gundyr -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The fight will start as soon as Gundyr is approached in his arena. He is vulnerable from the first moment and the player should take this opportunity to score as many hits as possible. It's not recommended to rush at him for this purpose, though, and instead conserve as much stamina as possible for when the battle properly starts.

Gundyr's most distinctive characteristic is his ability to dominate the immediate area around him. He has a vast repertoire of wide attacks and backward counter moves, and can also close the distance to the player in an instant. The main problem in this fight is Gundyr's excellent tracking, which allows him to unleash all of his attacks almost with perfect accuracy at the player, even if they roll away or are standing right behind him.

title: Soul of the Dancer
snippet:
Soul of the Dancer -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Obtained upon defeating the Dancer of the Boreal Valley in the High Wall of Lothric.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet:
Boreal Outrider Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Outrider Knights are usually initially unaware of the player, so use this opportunity to start the fight with a powerful attack. Once provoked, it is possible to wear them down with ranged weapons from a distance; however, they can close the gap very quickly so caution is advised. Unless the player has plenty of poise, it is recommended to evade their attacks rather than block them, as they rapidly drain stamina.

All of their attacks inflict Frost damage and can cause frostbite, which can be lethal if the player is unable to escape. They are very agile opponents and will often sidestep attacks, so a quick-use weapon is recommended.

When they are far away from the player, they are very susceptible to ranged attacks and will just continue approaching very slowly without attacking. Headshots are especially effective and will stagger them heavily.

title: Iron Dragonslayer
snippet:
Iron Dragonslayer -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The strategies employed against the boss version of the armour are equally effective against this version, as it begins the fight with its phase two moveset. The swamp gives the player more room to battle it, allowing for increased maneuverability. It is recommended to clear out any nearby enemies before approaching the Dragonslayer as they may prove to be a fatal distraction.

One trait about this enemy is that once it detects the player, it will pursue them relentlessly around the swamp, even inside the submerged shrine and into the chamber containing the bonfire. It is possible to lure the Dragonslayer onto the bridge where Darkeater Midir ambushes the player and use the dragon's fire breath to defeat it without having to engage it directly.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet:
Boreal Outrider Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - see_also 
 see_also : Vordt of the Boreal Valley

title: Dancer's Set
snippet:
Dancer's Set -  Dark Souls III - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : Possesses moderate all-round defenses, but is particularly weak to Strike and Fire damage. It has very weak Curse resistance, but can ward off Frost rather well.

title: Knight Slayer Tsorig
snippet:
Knight Slayer Tsorig -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Tsorig is a very dangerous enemy who can quickly dispose of any foe with just a few swings of his ultra greatsword. The player is advised to let him perform the first move and then counterattack, although only if they are sure he is not going to follow with another attack. In addition, the player should not get greedy and never attack him more than once or twice. His most powerful attacks have very slow buildup and will always leave him open afterward.

Special caution must be taken when he holds his ultra greatsword with both hands, as he can easily break guards and stagger the player, should any of his attacks connect.

title: Deacon
snippet:
Deacon -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Deacons are weak opponents and easily defeated with a few standard attacks. Their threat comes from the speed at which they cast their spells and how they often appear in large groups that can overwhelm the player with a constant barrage of fireballs. It is recommended to either thin them out with ranged attacks from a distance or use hit and run tactics to eliminate them one by one.

title: Basilisk (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Basilisk (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Basilisks are very slippery foes that can be hard to kill due to their evasiveness. Because they only possess breath attacks, they are incapable of damaging the player in any way short of inflicting the status effect.

Ideally, Basilisks should be engaged in a situation where the player has mobility options. Simply attack and kill a Basilisk while attempting to stay outside of the mist, and retreat as needed if Curse buildup becomes too high. Large weapons with high impact and stagger can lock down Basilisks long enough to finish them off. While weapons with horizontal sweep can allow the player to hit multiple targets at once, vertically attacking weapons can sometimes knock them out of the air as they perform pouncing attacks or jumping retreats.

title: Devout Bomber
snippet:
Devout Bomber -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Devout Bombers take a few seconds to ignite, which gives the player enough time to defeat them before they become a threat. Once ignited, they will attempt a dive bomb that can be easily evaded, although it does have limited tracking if the player moves too early. With careful positioning, they can be used to injure and even defeat nearby enemies.

title: Dancer's Gauntlets
snippet:
Dancer's Gauntlets -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : Gauntlets worn by the Dancer of the Boreal Valley.

The black eyes of the Pontiff eventually transformed the Dancer into a beastly creature, her armor fusing with her own hide.

title: Silver Knight Ledo
snippet:
Silver Knight Ledo -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Ledo will invade the player when they explore the tower above the Ringed City Streets. The small confines of the room make him particularly dangerous and he will likely kill the player swiftly if they are cornered. His hammer swings are slow but very powerful and will deplete virtually all stamina if blocked. If the player keeps their guard up for too long, he will use a guard break followed by an immediate swing that can instantly kill them.

Occasionally, Ledo will activate the skill of his hammer, Call to Stone, allowing him to perform spinning strikes that have the potential to wipe out the player in a single hit. Even if evaded, the area-of-effect blast at the end of the attack has a short stun effect that can prove deadly if Ledo is in attack range.

title: Rapier Champion
snippet:
Rapier Champion -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : A very dangerous enemy that can easily break through the strongest defenses. He has rather low poise, however, and this weakness should be exploited.

It is recommended to rush up to finish the Man Serpent Summoner first, as battling both enemies can be very risky. If this is not possible, the player may opt to lure the champion toward the Great Belfry, as the summoner will remain back and there will be no other enemies around, thus allowing to face him alone.

Alternatively, as soon as he is summoned, the player should begin combat with a backstab. Care should be taken, though, as most likely the summoner will start unleashing barrages of homing spells; the first of these may be completely negated if caught during the backstabbing animation, however.

If it's not possible to finish the champion after the initial attack, then the player should hurry in killing the summoner while he's still recovering.

title: Duke Tseldora
snippet:
Duke Tseldora -  Dark Souls II - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Giving him no quarter is the most effective way to beat him as he will have his back turned, leaving him open for a few easy hits and allowing him to be staggered rather easily, which means the player can easily staggerlock him to death.

title: Drang Knight
snippet:
Drang Knight -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Fighting these enemies can be dangerous due to all the hindrances present in the area where they are encountered. Three Deacons will be constantly shooting quick homing fireballs from a floor above, and two supposedly dead Giant Slaves will come to life and attack if approached. In addition, both Drang Knights will attack at the same time, even if only one was alerted.

Rather than confronting them head on, a safer strategy consists in entering a path located on the left side of the courtyard, where several Irithyllian Slaves are congregated; dispose of them first and then damage one of the knights with a ranged attack, thus luring them to fight in that enclosed area, away from the giants and the Deacons' fire.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beast -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : These beasts are very aggressive opponents and can easily kill the player if they are unable to escape their vicious assault. It is recommended to evade their attacks rather than block them, as they can deplete stamina very quickly and will often interrupt attempts to heal. Attacking them from the sides can prove effective as long as the player keeps away from their heads, as their bite has a long reach.

title: Dancer's Enchanted Swords
snippet:
Dancer's Enchanted Swords -  Dark Souls III - weapon - description 
 description : Paired enchanted swords that Pontiff Sulyvahn bestowed upon the Dancer of the Boreal Valley.
These blades, symbolic of the Dancer's vows, are enchanted with dark magic in the right-hand, and fire in the left, mirroring the Pontiff.

Skill: Dancer's Grace
Unleash the fury of both blades in a dancing spin motion and use strong attack to continue the performance until stamina is exhausted.

title: Silver Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Silver Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - particular_strategies 
 particular_strategies : around the knight, furthermore, they can be easily backstabbed this way by standing a bit closer to their left arm than the right.
|-|Spear=If the knight begins to charge for a lunge, an easy parry can follow suit: when the knight has closed the distance halfway to the player, execute the skill of your parrying tool.
On the other hand, if the knight instead of charging is *jogging* to you with shield in a diagonal position, prepare for a budge with the tip of the spear followed by a strong uprooting sweep. This attack can either be parried (just a pinch after the offender starts the animation for budge with the tip) or *sprinted* around the knight, possibly followed by a backstab.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : During the first phase, the player must defeat Lorian by dodging his attacks and attacking him during his recoveries. Good rolling is mandatory, as Lorian's attacks all deal extremely heavy damage and inflict Fire damage, meaning that even greatshields cannot completely mitigate damage. As Lorian's recovery windows are quite small, fast-swinging weapons such as straight swords are highly recommended in order to leave the player less vulnerable when Lorian begins attacking again.

Lorian is extremely weak to Lightning damage, so use of Gold Pine Resin or Lightning Blade can allow players to quickly pass through the first phase. As well, dealing enough damage to Lorian in a short amount of time will stagger him, allowing the player to riposte him from the front.

title: Fallen Knight
snippet:
Fallen Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The Fallen Knight can be very dangerous against unprepared players. His fighting methods are somewhat similar to Hodrick's. He dwells hidden at the end of a slope located to the left of the first bonfire upon arriving to the Cathedral of the Deep, and is intended to surprise the player from the rearguard while they are engaging the Brigand. Even alone, this enemy can be a major threat due to his advanced combat mechanics and high resilience.

When he switches to his dagger, raise a shield with good stability; upon hitting it, he will stagger and become open for a counterattack.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Knight Artorias -  Dark Souls III - boss - melee_strategy 
 melee_strategy : While this boss is rather difficult to predict, he does have a few signs for his attacks, and well-timed rolls prove useful here. Being able to fast-roll is highly advised but not necessary. The player can place themself away from him by about twice his reach at all times, even for melee.

title: Demon (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Demon (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Siegward of Catarina will help when the player starts the fight with the Demon in the Undead Settlement.
Skeletons in the Catacombs of Carthus will attack the Demon. For an easy kill, spawn as many skeletons while running past the Demon to the Abandoned Tomb bonfire.
**Alternatively to the skeletons, the Mimic located above will also attack it.

title: Monstrosity of Sin
snippet:
Monstrosity of Sin -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : These enemies are very slow but inflict heavy damage and have a large amount of vitality. They also react surprisingly fast at the player's attempts to keep some distance, diving, rolling and slamming their back to reach them. It is recommended to draw them out of the temple one at a time and slowly wear them down with ranged weapons from a distance.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : It is advised to finish the first phase quickly to conserve Estus for the second phase. This can be done by aiming to stagger the boss; by pressuring him and attacking constantly while avoiding its attacks, when it staggers there will be a brief window for a fully-charged strong attack. The boss won't stagger if the player gives it breathing room where its poise meter will fill up. However, beware that this strategy is difficult to pull off when the Soul of Cinder uses its Scimitar moveset, because he will start attacking in quick succession. Attacks with heavier weapons like Greataxes can stagger the boss within two to three repeated hits, in some cases with the weapon being wielded in one hand alone.

title: Silver Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Silver Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The Silver Knights within this game are much more powerful than their *Dark Souls* counterparts. For example, their arrows travel much faster than before, and they also attack much faster, utilizing their weapon arts. Therefore, the knights must be treated with great care, blocking is advised, but rolling away from their attacks is better.

title: Iudex Gundyr
snippet:
Iudex Gundyr -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Gundyr cannot be damaged until the Coiled Sword has been removed from his chest. Once done, he will begin to rise and is vulnerable to damage, even though his health bar won't appear until he has taken up his weapon. This allows the player to deal substantial damage at the beginning of the fight without Gundyr retaliating.

While his attacks seem menacing and aggressive, most of them have poor tracking, are very slow, and are also amply telegraphed. Retaining a medium distance from him will help to avoid his attacks accordingly. Rolling either behind him, through his attacks or both will allow the player to punish Gundyr with several hits at a time.

title: Thrall
snippet:
Thrall -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Individually, Thralls are very small threats, their real danger lies in their tendency to mob players or ambush them while aided by other enemies. If the player senses a trap, it is best to step forward to trigger the ambush, and then immediately roll away and retreat to more favorable terrain, where the Thralls must all attack from a single direction.

Always keep an eye on the surrounding areas, especially above or below. Thralls can often be seen hanging from ceilings or walls, a sure sign of a trap. Using a bow to hit them will cause them to immediately drop down or climb up and attack, allowing crafty players to thin out potential ambushes one by one and greatly reducing the threat they pose.

title: Longfinger Kirk
snippet:
Longfinger Kirk -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Invades once the player reaches the central cloistered area on the first floor of the cathedral, spawning on the opposite corridor. A Thrall will be patrolling on the left side, so it is advised to take it out first lest it meddles during the fight.

The player may start attacking Kirk at a distance as soon as he finishes spawning, although after being hit once or twice he will start evading most attacks.

While coming equipped with a shield, Kirk will rely more on an offensive approach. Since he keeps his defenses down for most of the fight, the player may take the first step and receive him with a two-handed attack. He will frequently use Stance in an attempt to break through the player's defenses. Lure him into attacking and make him miss, then counterattack.

title: Dancer's Set
snippet:
Dancer's Set -  Dark Souls III - armor - availability 
 availability : Purchased from the Shrine Handmaid for a total of 31,000 souls after defeating the Dancer of the Boreal Valley.

title: Peasant Hollow
snippet:
Peasant Hollow -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Peasant Hollows have low health and are easy to stagger. They often appear in small groups, so it is recommended to wear them down with ranged weapons as they close in. The red eyed variant has slightly larger health and is more aggressive, but overall the same strategy still applies.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Balder Knights have a fair amount of health, and are a considerable threat to new characters. Even one-on-one, they can be very dangerous.

Any ranged attack is useful against them, but they are fast and will close the gap quickly. Firebombs can be very useful in defeating them.

Critical attacks, such as the Parry and Riposte and Backstab, are exceedingly efficient methods to dispatch these enemies.

title: Forest Hunter Knight
snippet:
Forest Hunter Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The knights are relentless and can hit for high damage against lower-vitality players, but they are hindered by trees and hills. A relatively easy method of fighting them is to lure them to the doorway to this area (the one needing the Crest of Artorias), as it allows for a more traditional combat arena, and then repeatedly parrying their attacks.

title: Bowman Guthry
snippet:
Bowman Guthry -  Dark Souls II - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Staying close to her will make it hard for her to land any shots on the player.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - first_phase_sister_friede 
 first_phase_sister_friede : First of all, it is suggested to use a light weapon (such as a straight sword, a greatsword, etc.) to avoid the risk of being stun-locked by her fast attacks, and also a greatshield with high stability to minimize some stamina damage.

After the beginning of the fight, be careful and learn her attack patterns while blocking with your shield (be careful anyway, because her scythe inflicts Magic damage).

Note that Friede will nearly always jump away after one or two hits, so it is not advised to go for more as it is very easy to disregard stamina and become open for a devastating counterattack. While she seems to have very little poise, she sometimes will almost completely ignore the player's attacks and poise through them with no trouble, guaranteeing the player gets hit if they are getting greedy.

title: High Wall of Lothric
snippet:
Towards the end of the area, the player will encounter High Priestess Emma, who grants them the Small Lothric Banner and Way of Blue covenant.

The area has two bosses: Vordt of the Boreal Valley, who guards the entrance to the Undead Settlement, and the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, who guards the entrance to Lothric Castle. Although the Dancer is intended to be fought much later in the game, players can face her early by killing Emma.

title: Bonfire (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
***Dancer of the Boreal Valley**
:Once the player is returned to the cathedral where they first met Priestess Emma, after having defeated the first three Lords of Cinder, she will die gifting the player the Basin of Vows. When approaching the statue behind her to place the basin, the Dancer of the Boreal Valley will enter the scene and her boss fight will take place. The bonfire will appear upon her defeat.

***Oceiros, the Consumed King**
:After defeating the Dancer of the Boreal Valley and placing the Basin of Vows, the player can ascend the ladder to Lothric Castle. Heading left from here and descending a lift leads to the Consumed King's Garden. Fighting through this area ultimately leads to the boss room for Oceiros, the Consumed King; the bonfire will appear upon defeating him.

title: Old Dragonslayer
snippet:
Old Dragonslayer -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The fight is very similar to the Dragonslayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough battle without Smough. There are slight differences in how the Old Dragonslayer fights compared to Ornstein. An example would be that the Old Dragonslayer uses a dark magic attack, while Ornstein uses lightning. Otherwise, Old Dragonslayer has the same sort of movement and similar attack patterns as Ornstein in the original *Dark Souls* should the player slay Executioner Smough first. If one takes his time fighting him, he will shoot three dark magic orbs at the player from the tip of his spear.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : At some point in time, after her younger brother Dark Sun Gwyndolin assumed the title of "Chief Deity" and built Irithyll of the Boreal Valley on the ruins of Anor Londo to house the descendants of the gods, she returned to her ancient home. Here the goddess was venerated with multiple statues displayed throughout the city and became the progenitor of several children with royal blood such as Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth and the Dancer of the Boreal Valley. The goddess would return to her quarters in the old cathedral of Anor Londo, protected by the remaining Silver Knights who had once protected her illusion and whose shields she would once again bless. Eventually she also left Irithyll, leaving her Sun Princess Ring behind.

title: Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle
snippet:
Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : High Priestess Emma presents the player with the Small Lothric Banner when she is first talked to, an item which grants passage to the Undead Settlement. She also lets the player join the Way of Blue covenant, upon talking to her a second time.

After defeating the first three Lords of Cinder, she will give the player the Basin of Vows, which is used to trigger the appearance of the Dancer of the Boreal Valley. She also drops the Basin if killed at any time, allowing the Dancer to be encountered early.

title: Silvercat Ring (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Silvercat Ring (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - ring - availability 
 availability : Obtained as a gift from Sirris in Firelink Shrine after helping her defeat Creighton in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

To perform this task, the player must look for Sirris's summon sign near the first half of the bridge that connects the Irithyll of the Boreal Valley bonfire to Central Irithyll and answer her call. If successful, the next time they visit Firelink Shrine, she will greet and thank them for their help, bestowing the ring as a reward.

title: Creighton the Wanderer (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Creighton the Wanderer (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : A former knight of Mirrah who deserted the order and became a ruthless criminal, Creighton eventually joined Rosaria's Fingers and became a target for Sirris. Eventually, he invades her as a dark spirit in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley and is defeated by her and the Ashen One.

Creighton later invades the player's world in revenge if he was defeated in the first encounter. Defeating him here awards the player with the Dragonslayer's Axe and causes a corpse to appear on the bridge into Irithyll with the Mirrah Chain Set.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : When Lucatiel is found for the first time, she will introduce herself and explain her motives for being in Drangleic. She will also offer her assistance to the player during their journey.

During her second encounter, Lucatiel will tell the player about her past in Mirrah. She will then take off her mask, revealing her partly hollowed visage, and give the player a Human Effigy, while claiming not to even know what it is.

The third time she is met, she tells the player about her fears of losing her memories and of her brother. Lucatiel will explain how he is a better swordsman than her and she confesses that her brother, who is another victim of the curse of undeath, might be in Drangleic. She then gifts the Ring of Steel Protection +1.

title: Goddess Fina
snippet:
Goddess Fina -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Legends of Fina and her fickle love survive to the time of Lothric, as well as the tales of the pitiable Embraced Knight who served her blindly, deluded by his own adoration. Her worship has also endured the test of time, but it appears to be most prominent in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city of the gods' descendants. Many of her blessed rings can be found there, but unlike the ones found in the past, they don't break when they are removed.

title: Lothric
snippet:
Vordt was sent to Lothric as a companion to the Dancer of the Boreal Valley. The Dancer is a direct descendant of Gwynevere, and was among the Irithyllians (Human and God hybrid) to inhabit Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Once the Pontiff took control of the city, he initially ordered the daughter of Gwynevere to serve as his personal "dancer". Later, he bestowed upon her two enchanted swords, mirroring the design of his own blades, along with the same ring given to other Outrider Knights. He then sent her to Lothric, which was his equivalent of exile. She positioned herself in the cathedral to guard High Priestess Emma and the entrance to Lothric Castle.

----

Despite the great losses of the regular army, the knights managed to regroup and maintain key positions in the city, rallying to protect the Cathedral and the High Priestess Emma, securing the military barracks and the Castle.

title: Shadow Set (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The leggings outclass the Conjurator Boots and the Worker Trousers.

If the player is skilled enough and manages to defeat the Dancer of the Boreal Valley early in the game, they can then head to the Consumed King's Garden and get their hands on this set near the beginning of a playthrough, potentially benefiting from its special features even before exploring the Undead Settlement.
